newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel wins Indonesian satellite order.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel wins Indonesian satellite order.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom said it had won from Space Systems/Loral a contract to build and place in orbit a satellite for Indonesia's Pasifik Satelit Nusantara (PSN).
Alcatel said the total deal was worth $350 million, including $100 million for the French company.
The satellite, Multi Media Asia or M2A, will be used for telecommunications as well as new multimedia offers such as video conferencing and data transfer as well as Internet traffic.
The contract includes preparations for the launch of a second satellite in the short term and an option to go to a total of five satellites.
M2A will cover China, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Thailand, Philippines, Australia and the Indian continent.
The first satellite will be launched in 1999.
